_readme: Single source of truth for the desktop shell's cross-language vocabulary. It holds the Tauri event names the Rust shell emits and the webview listens for. It holds the env vars Rust passes to the Go sidecar at spawn; the sidecar reads LEAPMUX_DESKTOP_DEV_ENDPOINT, LEAPMUX_DESKTOP_BINARY_HASH, and (debug only) LEAPMUX_HUB_DEV_FRONTEND so TCP extra listen addresses reverse-proxy to the Vite/Bun server the webview already uses. It also holds the frame cap both programs enforce on the sidecar IPC wire. The cap must exceed channelwire.UserEventsReadLimit plus the Frame/Event envelope; frame_test.go's full-size-bootstrap test pins that floor. It also holds windowBehavior, the enum tokens of the Desktop account settings: those tokens are the one part of a user setting that a THIRD language must spell, because the Rust shell matches tray_on_close, tray_on_minimize and start_minimized out of the set_desktop_behavior payload to decide what a window close, a window minimize and a login launch do. The hub states them once in usersettings/keys.go (the enum catalogue and the validator both derive from these constants) and the webview states them once in its device-tier parse. The block NESTS one object per setting, so the schema enforces the grouping and the generator's per-setting uniqueness rule reads straight off it; the emitted constant names stay flat, the same split flattenWire makes for wire.json. It also holds launchVisibility, the three tokens the shell reports through get_startup_info and the webview reads in parseLaunchVisibility to decide whether to show the window: a Rust-and-TS pair like tauriEvents, and one that drifts in SILENCE without a contract, because that parse answers normal for every token it does not recognize. It also holds windowMode, the saved display state of the main window, which all THREE languages spell -- the Go config persists it, the Rust shell matches it at launch, and the webview reads and writes it through save_window_geometry. These four blocks are the whole vocabulary of the desktop config: every token on that wire is a contract token, and no proto enum restates one. The Tauri COMMAND name and its argument names stay out, like every other Tauri command's. task generate-contracts emits a Rust module (desktop/rust/src/generated/contracts.rs), Go constants (the sidecar's main.go and the hub's usersettings read them), and the TS names the webview subscribes and parses with. The named-pipe and unix-socket endpoint NAMES are deliberately NOT here: only Rust constructs them, handing the endpoint to the Go sidecar through the env var. No second language spells them, so there is no mirror to hold. maxFrameSizeBytes rides the Go and Rust outputs only, like the env vars.
